lesson.menu_desc: Commanding language for a high-stakes talk: the more..., the more... -- a hook, a soundbite and a call to action at the global town hall
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 26 -- Executive Presence -- Comparative correlatives (the more..., the more...) for strong conclusions
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Fabiana Michelly Silva | Lesson 26 -- Executive Presence

listenings.text: Hi Fabiana, it's Priya. First of all, congratulations. The board approved the dual-supplier contract this morning, and several people mentioned how well you handled the rapid round. Now I have a bigger stage for you. Next Thursday is the global operations town hall, with about three hundred people in twelve countries. I'd like you to speak for five minutes about what the Penang fire taught us. This is not a status update. The audience doesn't need every number. They need one clear message and a reason to act. The more you tell it as a story, the more it will resonate. Please end with a call to action for every team, not just supply chain. If you want a model, listen to the talk Tom Becker gave last year. Send me your opening line by Monday, and we'll do a quick rehearsal on Wednesday.

Good morning, everyone. A few years ago, a single container ship got stuck in a canal, and for six days, the world's supply chains held their breath. We were lucky. We had three weeks of inventory. Many companies had three days. So today I want to leave you with one idea. The more connected we are, the more fragile we become, unless we plan for it. Resilience is not a project. It is not a department. It is a habit. And habits are built in quiet weeks, not in crisis weeks. So here is my ask. Before the end of this quarter, every team will name one single point of failure, one person who owns it, and one plan to remove it. The sooner we start, the less we will pay later. Thank you.

extra_audio.text: Fabiana plans her five-minute town hall talk. She opens with one image: last July, a fire in Penang stopped our keyboard supply for twelve days. She pauses for effect and lets the image land. She tells one story with three lessons: map, diversify, rehearse. She gives the soundbite: the longer we depended on one supplier, the bigger the risk became. And she closes with a call to action: the sooner every team maps its suppliers, the safer we all are.
